flags.flag: QUANTIFIER?: θ is existential inside the witness, so 'explicitly described permutations' is stated as 'some partition labelling of the nondescent permutations' — the explicit labelling of the paper is not pinned by the statement (the positivity claim is unaffected).
flags.why: The labelling θ is existential, but this does not drop any truth condition of the headline. The statement fixes the counted objects explicitly: permutations whose consecutive descents are G-edges (Nondescent). It fixes their q-weights (graphInversions) and requires that the fibres of θ partition them into the e_λ coefficients for every number r of variables, which pins the symmetric-function identity. So the ℕ[q] e-positivity (sentence 1) is fully stated, and so is the content of sentence 2: each coefficient is a q-count of a set of explicitly defined permutations with an explicit statistic, and the sets partition the nondescent permutations. That is stronger than bare positivity, since it fixes Σ_λ c_λ(q). What is left open is the paper's particular rule for θ, which is a property of the proof, not a mathematical claim. θ ranges over a finite set, and the identity is decidable (it suffices at r = n), so a θ exists iff a computable one does (the first in any enumeration). 'Explicitly described' therefore adds no truth condition the Lean misses. The witness is a def, so the solution supplies an actual θ; lane K: CERTIFIED, strict run SAME BODIES.

flags.flag: JUNK? (low): trialLog and functional are Bochner integrals over the nested weak-topology hierarchy. An integrand that is not AE-strongly measurable integrates to 0 and could pull phi r below the true infimum. That would make the Lean equality FALSE, not weaker. I argued measurability by continuity of eta -> logMean on the Polish hierarchy spaces (induction on r) but did not verify it line by line. Lean: ComparatorChallenges/DilutedSpin.lean:111-113, 119-120.
flags.why: No Bochner junk can occur, and the first reader's open measurability point closes. (1) Every integrand in the functional is bounded, independently of the trial law ζ. q(x,·) is a probability vector (e^{±x}/(2cosh x)), so edge θ x and the sum inside message are convex combinations of e^{θ(s)}. That gives |log edge θ x| ≤ ‖θ‖ and |message| ≤ ‖θ‖. siteLog is the log of an average over ε, so |siteLog θ h x| ≤ |h| + Σ_j ‖θ_j.1‖. logMean preserves a bound C at every level (a log-power-mean with m 0 > 0 by Exponents), so heavy-tailed ζ cannot make anything non-integrable. The outer integrals are dominated by |h| + Σ_j‖θ_j‖ and ‖θ‖, which are integrable by interaction_integrable and field_integrable against a Poisson number of terms (finite mean). (2) Measurability: siteLog and log∘edge are continuous in the messages. Each Hierarchy r is Polish (ℝ, then P(Polish) with the weak topology; the σ-algebra is Borel either way). For bounded continuous F, η ↦ ∫F d(⊗_i η_i) is weakly continuous on finite products of separable metric spaces, so by induction η ↦ logMean r g m η is continuous, hence Borel. (3) pressure is genuine: |logPartition| ≤ N log 2 + Σ_j‖θ_j.1‖ + Σ_i|h_i|, continuous, integrable. So phi r is the infimum of a genuine, finite functional. Because the left side is genuine, any residual junk on the right could only make the equality false. Lane K: CERTIFIED.

flags.flag: VACUITY? (low): all_grid_moment is conditional on ScaleLarge, SparseScalar.ScaleReady, MainSizeReady for every allowed grid and SparsePerturb; read as jointly satisfiable for large r (finitely many grids with b ≤ 12800 for SparsePerturb; size conditions hold for large sizes); conditional_main is unconditional
flags.why: The hypotheses of all_grid_moment are jointly satisfiable, so it is not vacuous. ScaleLarge r needs r·log 2 ≥ (2/e0)² = 4·10⁸, which holds for large r. ScaleReady r needs r·log 2 ≥ 8(3 log 2 + 2(K0+1+log 4))/θ ≈ 2.6·10⁹, plus SizeReady s for every s ≥ 2^r. Each SizeReady clause (log s ≤ s^{θ/4}, 2 ≤ s^{θ/4}, B0+1 ≤ s^{θ/2}, the count, absorb, η, prefactor (needs log s ≳ 4·10¹⁹) and logtwo clauses) holds for all s past a finite threshold and stays true, so r ≳ 10²⁰ suffices. MainSizeReady q (G.size) holds for every allowed G because G.size ≥ 2^r (b ≥ 1, bits ≥ r) and each of its four clauses holds for all large s. SparsePerturb r zStar: slack(G.size) > 0 since G.size > 1; at z = 0 every eventDistance is 0, since choiceWeight 0 > 0 makes each denominator positive; eventDistance is continuous in z near 0. There are finitely many grids (b ≤ 12800, r ≤ bits ≤ 2r) and finitely many nonempty E ⊆ G.Choices, so some δ > 0 works uniformly, and zStar = min(δ, baseZeta r) > 0 qualifies. conditional_main has no hypotheses, so it is unaffected.

The inner fallback in smearedMap (else 0 unless ∀ v, Summable) is also dead: for v ∈ V, ‖f̂(m)·a_{m+d−1}v‖ ≤ ‖f̂(m)‖·C(1+|m+d−1|)^p·‖(1+L0)^k v‖ (the energy bound) is summable against rapid decay, and Completion V is complete, so the family is norm-summable. So if the theorem holds, every smeared field is the genuine tsum Σ f̂(m) a_{m+d−1}; if conjunct 1 failed, the theorem would be false. The net is never trivialized by this junk.

flags.flag: JUNK? (not triggered): resolvent, flow and projectiveStandardAction are defined by h.choose with fallbacks 0, 0, 1; the defining existentials hold for self-adjoint generators and the Möbius action, and a fallback for projectiveStandardAction would force a one-dimensional Hilbert space (vacuum_unique), i.e. falsity rather than weakness
flags.why: None of the three existentials fails, so no fallback is reached. (1) resolvent: hamiltonian_selfAdjoint is Mathlib's IsSelfAdjoint for a LinearPMap (T† = T), which forces a dense domain (Mathlib's IsSelfAdjoint.dense_domain) and closedness. So T is a genuine self-adjoint operator, and for |Im z| ≥ 1 the bounded R = (T−z)⁻¹ satisfies (R y, y + z R y) ∈ graph T, uniquely since T−z is injective. (2) flow: boundedGenerator(r) = (r²/2)((T−ir)⁻¹ + (T+ir)⁻¹) = r²T/(T²+r²), and exp(it·B_n) → e^{itT} strongly by spectral dominated convergence, so the limit L exists, is unique, and equals e^{itT}. (3) projectiveStandardAction: every M ∈ SL(2,ℝ) acts on the circle by the doubled-angle Möbius map, an orientation-preserving smooth diffeomorphism with a smooth 2π-equivariant lift F satisfying Implements M F. Rel M x y fixes y mod 2π, so the class of F in Group (lifts modulo the kernel of the circle action) depends only on M, and −1 acts trivially. The lifts proof shows products implement products, so the homomorphism exists and is unique. The first reader's backstop also checks out: fallback 0 for flow contradicts rotation_flow (isometries on H ≠ 0, vacuum_norm = 1), and fallback 1 for projectiveStandardAction makes extends_mobius force mobius F to be scalar, hence trivial (PSL(2,ℝ) is perfect), hence by vacuum_unique dim H = 1. Both would be falsity, never weakness.

flags.flag: JUNK? (not triggered): moduli are nested real sInf/sSup; in an infinite-dimensional space with an equivalent norm the inner sets are nonempty and lie in [−1,t] (AUC) or [0,t] (averaged), so no junk value can occur
flags.why: The direction that matters is ¬IsAUC: a junk 0 in aucModulus would make it trivially true. It cannot occur. Conjunct 1 asserts FullDual Vertex is infinite-dimensional, so every closed finite-codimensional F is infinite-dimensional, hence nonzero. N is a norm (α‖x‖ ≤ N x with α > 0), so F contains N-unit vectors and aucValues/averageValues are nonempty. For N x = N y = 1 and t > 0: N(x+ty)−1 ∈ [−1, t] (it is in fact ≥ |t−1|−1), and (N(x+ty)+N(x−ty))/2 − 1 ∈ [0, t] by the triangle inequality. So each inner sInf is a true infimum. The outer range is nonempty (F = the whole space is in Cofinite) and bounded above by t, so the sSup is true. The outermost set is nonempty (unit vectors exist) and bounded below (−1 or 0), so the sInf is true. ¬IsAUC therefore asserts a genuinely nonpositive modulus at some t > 0, and the averaged lower bound √(1+t²/12)−1 > 0 is compared with the true modulus.

flags.flag: JUNK? checked, none: derivWithin/fderiv would be 0 at non-differentiable points, but every solution is ContDiffOn ℝ 1 on the closed half-space, so the derivatives in the equations are genuine; ρ and j are Bochner integrals of compactly supported continuous integrands.
flags.why: The derivatives in Equations are genuine. Classical requires ContDiffOn ℝ 1 for f, E and B on the closed half-space {t ≥ 0}, which is convex with nonempty interior, hence UniqueDiffOn. So derivWithin … (Ici 0) t is the true (one-sided at t = 0) time derivative. The spatial and velocity fderiv of the slices y ↦ s.f(t,y,v), v' ↦ s.f(t,x,v'), y ↦ s.E(t,y) are true derivatives even at t = 0: those slices map into the half-space, and the within-derivative there is unique. ρ and j are Bochner integrals of v ↦ s.f(t,x,v) (times |velocity v| < 1). That slice is continuous (from ContDiffOn) and compactly supported (CompactOnFiniteHorizons), so it is integrable, and the same holds for f₀ in Admissible (ContDiff with HasCompactSupport). So existence cannot be satisfied by junk-zero derivatives or integrals. On the uniqueness side, junk could only enlarge the class of 'classical' s′, which makes uniqueness stronger, not weaker.
